req.title: Redirect-to accepts POST as well
req.statement: The system shall accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE on /redirect-to.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE methods. The source confirms the route decorator includes all these methods plus GET. Tests must verify: (1) each method returns a redirect status (302 by default), (2) the Location header is set exactly to the supplied URL, (3) custom status_code parameter works at boundaries (300, 399), (4) unsupported methods (e.g., HEAD without explicit support beyond Flask defaults) and missing 'url' parameter yield errors. The source reads 'url' from request.args (query string) for all methods, so all methods must pass url as a query parameter. Mutation-resilient assertions check exact status codes, exact Location header values, and boundary status_code values.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_post_default_302
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_post_default_302():
    r = client.post('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_post_default_302()
